en: The Apadāna of the Elder Dhātupūjaka Tuvaradāyaka Chapter 7.7 I offered a bowl of curdled milk to the Buddha, the Teacher, who was seated beneath the Ajapāla banyan tree. Because of that deed, I have attained the fruit of Stream-entry (sotāpatti-phala). May I never again fall into the states of woe. Through this merit, may I attain final Nibbāna. May I never again be born into a womb. May I never again be subject to old age. May I never again be subject to death. May I never again be subject to suffering. May I never again be subject to defilements. May I never again be subject to rebirth. May I never again be subject to the round of existence. May I never again be subject to the cycle of birth and death. May I never again be subject to the ocean of saṃsāra. May I never again be subject to the abyss of existence. May I never again be subject to the mire of craving. May I never again be subject to the thicket of views. May I never again be subject to the net of Māra. May I never again be subject to the snare of the Evil One. May I never again be subject to the darkness of ignorance. May I never again be subject to the blindness of delusion. May I never again be subject to the fetters of attachment. May I never again be subject to the bonds of aversion. May I never again be subject to the shackles of pride. May I never again be subject to the chains of envy. May I never again be subject to the yoke of conceit. May I never again be subject to the weight of lust. May I never again be subject to the burden of hatred. May I never again be subject to the obstacle of delusion. May I never again be subject to the hindrance of doubt. May I never again be subject to the obstruction of sloth and torpor. May I never again be subject to the veil of restlessness and remorse. May I never again be subject to the covering of ignorance. May I never again be subject to the accumulation of kamma. May I never again be subject to the ripening of results. May I never again be subject to the arising of suffering. May I never again be subject to the cessation of happiness. May I never again be subject to the descent into the lower realms. May I never again be subject to the ascent into the higher realms. “When Siddhattha, the supreme among men, the Lord of the World, had entered Nibbāna,
Of the Lord of bipeds, the Tathāgata.
Having taken that relic of the Buddha,
For five years I served the Supreme among Men as he stood firm;
Because I worshipped that relic at that time,
I do not know a state of misery;
such is the fruit of attending upon a relic.
[and so forth] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Dhātupūjaka spoke these verses.
This is the seventh legend of the elder Dhātupūjaka.
